newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money rates slump, gilt yields steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money rates slump, gilt yields steady.

text.p: Indian call money closed at 9.75-10.25 percent on Monday against the day's opening of 10.25-10.50 percent, dealers said.
"The market was easy, call rates fell to 9.50-10 percent," said a dealer at Centurion Bank. "The securities market was dull and the market is awaiting the zero coupon bond issue results."
A handful of banks were hunting for funds, which moved up the call rates from 9.50 percent to 10 percent on the closing session, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to announce the results of a sale of zero coupon bonds later on Monday.
Many dealers said the bonds would be fully subscribed and expected them to be traded in the secondary market at 60.40-60.50 rupees levels against the issue price of 60.66.

"The security market witnessed a slight upward trend but it was not much compared to last week's rally," said Mithi Somesh at Lloyds Brokerage Ltd. He said the trading was restricted to the short-dated securities.
Jatin Thakkar at Mukesh Babu Securities Ltd said there were no trades on treasury bills on Monday.
He said the total volume transacted on the National Stock Exchange was 982.10 million rupees on Monday against Saturday's volume of 1.25 billion rupees.
Inter-corporate deposit rates were steady at 18-19.5 percent for blue-chip companies and commercial papers (CP) were quoted at 13.50-14.00 for P1+ companies, a dealer said.
